record.original_question: How can complex biological systems with nonlinear dynamics and stochastic effects be modeled and analyzed so that one can predict when deterministic qualitative features such as bistability, stationarity, or bifurcations survive the introduction of noise, and how can one build approximations that remain reliable in nonlinear stochastic regimes?

evidence.quote: This lack of conservation of qualitative features of dynamical systems — including number and nature of stationary states, existence of bifurcations, etc, — as noise is introduced, or more precisely our inability to predict a priori if qualitative features are conserved upon the introduction of noise, is becoming a limiting factor in many analyses.
In short, we do not understand anywhere near enough how to model, analyse, and understand complex dynamical systems that are subject to stochastic effects.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a deterministic dynamical system on $\mathbb{R}^n$ of the form $\dot{x} = f(x;\lambda)$, where $f:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^n$ is smooth and $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^k$ is a parameter. Such systems may exhibit qualitative features such as: (i) multiple isolated equilibria (bistability or multistability), (ii) stationary states with prescribed stability type, and (iii) bifurcations (saddle-node, Hopf, pitchfork, etc.) at critical parameter values. Now introduce stochastic perturbations to obtain a stochastic differential equation
$$dX_t = f(X_t;\lambda)\,dt + \sigma\, g(X_t;\lambda)\,dW_t,$$
where $W_t$ is a standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion, $g:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$ is smooth, and $\sigma>0$ controls the noise intensity. The problem is:

(a) Develop a general framework giving verifiable a priori criteria, in terms of $f$, $g$, and $\sigma$, under which the qualitative features of the deterministic system (number and nature of stationary states, existence and type of bifurcations, bistability) are preserved by the stochastic system in a precise sense (e.g., existence of a corresponding number of metastable states of the invariant measure, stochastic bifurcation in the sense of Lyapunov exponents or invariant measure topology, peak structure of the stationary density).

(b) Construct systematic approximation schemes (beyond linear-noise / van Kampen system-size expansion, small-noise large deviation, and moment closure) that remain quantitatively reliable in nonlinear stochastic regimes where the noise is not asymptotically small and the drift is genuinely nonlinear, with rigorous error bounds.

State and prove such criteria and approximations, or establish obstructions showing that no such general framework can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad research-program-level open question on the modeling and analysis of nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems in mathematical biology. While many partial results exist (Freidlin–Wentzell large deviations, stochastic bifurcation theory, linear-noise approximations, chemical Langevin equation, moment closures), no general framework predicting a priori which deterministic qualitative features survive noise is known. The problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology (zbMATH listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems including modeling complex biological systems with nonlinear dynamics and stochastic effects.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey of open problems in mathematical biology.
